label: Best friend relation removed
summary: Runs when a character loses a best friend relation because it expired.
details: The character who owned the relation is the root, and the former best friend is `scope:target`. The vanilla comment says it is not fired on death, only when the relationship runs out. Vanilla uses it to take away the strong hooks that Ritualised Friendship gives best friends, and to remove the friendship synergy bonus modifiers from both characters, each with a toast message.

label: Blood brother relation removed
summary: Runs when a character stops being blood brother to another character.
details: `scope:target` is the other blood brother; vanilla saves it as `other_blood_brother`. Vanilla removes the blood brother modifiers and the blood brother family opinion from the root. It does the same for the root's spouses and children who hold that opinion of the other brother. If the two are allied, it also breaks that alliance.

label: Disciple relation removed
summary: Runs when a character loses a disciple relation.
details: Vanilla goes through the fellow-disciple relations of `scope:target` and removes each one. So the target is most likely the disciple who left, and the root the elder (the matching set action counts the root's disciples). This direction is inferred from vanilla's use, not stated by the game.

label: Friend relation removed
summary: Runs when a character loses a friend relation because it expired.
details: The root owned the relation and `scope:target` was the friend. The vanilla comment says it is not fired on death. Vanilla removes the confidants perk modifier from the root, and from the friend if the friend has the perk. It fires a death management event for both, removes decentralized rule effects from the friend, and gives each of them a memory of the friendship ending.

label: Grudge relation removed
summary: Runs when a character loses a grudge relation with another character.
details: The root owns the relation and `scope:target` is the other character. The game does not say who held the grudge against whom. Vanilla only gives the root a memory that the grudge ended.

label: Guardian relation removed
summary: Runs when a ward loses their guardian, or is about to die.
details: The root is the ward and `scope:target` is the guardian. If the ward has a liege, vanilla removes the opinions linked to the guardianship. A ward who is a foreign court guest and is not at their own liege's court is sent back home. If both sides are in a struggle phase that applies a truce when sending wards, and the guardian has a truce with the ward's liege, that truce is cancelled both ways.

label: Lover relation removed
summary: Runs when a character stops being lover to another character.
details: The root is the character losing the relation and `scope:target` is the former lover. Vanilla runs the lose-lover effect, makes the target the character's old flame (if they are not one already), and gives both a memory of the break-up.

label: Rival relation removed
summary: Runs when a character stops being rival to another character.
details: The root is the character losing the relation and `scope:target` is the former rival. Vanilla gives both of them a memory that they stopped being rivals. An event call is commented out in the file.

label: Ward relation removed
summary: Runs for the guardian when they lose a ward.
details: The root is the guardian and `scope:target` is the ward. If the guardian has a liege, vanilla removes the opinions linked to the guardianship. Then the guardian, if a foreign court guest, is sent back home unless the court is their liege's, they are a playable character, or they are at the court of another of their wards. A comment in the file says this part should not be needed.

label: Character changes rite
summary: Runs when a character changes their faith or rite.
details: The root is the character. `scope:old_faith` is the faith they had, and `scope:old_rite` the rite they had (it can be the same as the current one). It does not run when a character gets a faith at birth, creation or similar. Vanilla handles conversion effects, updates the coats of arms of their titles, flags the character, creates a conversion memory and triggers struggle catalysts and effects for some struggles. The input cuts the script off, so more may follow.

label: Character creates a rite
summary: Runs when a character creates a new rite.
details: The root is the creator. `scope:old_faith` and `scope:old_rite` are what they had before. Vanilla treats everyone in the faith who already holds the new rite as part of the founding wave and converts their court, and their domain counties if they hold a county or higher. It sets a grace period variable and a one year founding window variable on the rite, and may change the opening chapter of a promoted legend (sometimes only with a 75% chance). A comment says rite growth and heresy events set the same grace variable, because `create_dynamic_rite` skips this on_action. The input cuts the script off.

label: Rite edit committed
summary: Runs right away when an edit made in the rite editor, which changed tenets or doctrines, is applied.
details: The root is the rite that was edited. Vanilla uses it to mark the head of the rite as having edited a rite, so that the once-per-lifetime edit lock is set before the editor can be reopened. The game warns not to misuse it and points to `on_rite_updated` for other uses.

label: Rite updated
summary: Runs after a rite has been changed.
details: The root is the rite. `scope:changed_tenets_or_doctrines` is set when tenets or doctrines changed, and `scope:consume_rite_edit_token` only when a player edited through the interface. Lists `added_tenets`, `removed_tenets`, `added_doctrines`, `removed_doctrines` and `changed_tenet_status` say exactly what changed. Vanilla picks an icon from these lists and sends an update message to the players of that rite, but stays silent while an ecumenical council of the faith is ongoing unless a player edited the rite. A second definition in the same file adds the on_action `pam_personal_tenet_status_change_fulfillment_on_action`.

label: Rite yearly
summary: Runs once a year for every rite.
details: The root is the rite. Vanilla uses it for two yearly effects of its own, one for passive learning and one for divergence drift.

label: Ruler designer finished
summary: Runs when a new character made in the ruler designer has been created.
details: The root is the new character. `scope:ruler_designer` says the type: `flag:landed_title`, `flag:landless_adventurer` or `flag:landless_noble_family`. Vanilla suppresses marriage events for some rites, adds children and incapable characters to a list of those needing a regency, gives the Hajjaj trait to someone starting in Mecca under a rite with mandatory Hajj, and sets up the adventurer title or noble family. Noble families also get 100 gold and an employer. It also resets and recalculates the character's prestige. The input cuts the script off.

label: Scheme agent discovered
summary: Runs when an agent of a scheme is exposed.
details: The root is the scheme and `scope:agent` is the exposed agent. Vanilla defines it with nothing in it.

label: Scheme discovered
summary: Runs when a scheme is discovered.
details: The root is the scheme. If the scheme's target character is a courtier at a court they do not own, and the host has reason to protect them (an heir who is a player, a consort, a character with a good relationship, or a ward who likes the host), vanilla adds the target to a list on the host for 10 years. There is one list for murder schemes and one for seduction schemes. For the Celestial treasury siphon scheme against the Chinese hegemony title, the scheme owner triggers a governor embezzlement catalyst against the hegemon, and loses legitimacy if they hold that title themselves.

label: Scheme opportunity changed
summary: Runs when a scheme's opportunity value changes.
details: `scope:scheme` is the scheme, and `scope:old_value` and `scope:new_value` hold the value before and after. When the new value crosses one of four thresholds, vanilla sends the scheme owner a message about the matching ending buff (tier 1 to 4).

label: Best friend relation set
summary: Runs when a character gets a best friend.
details: The root is the character and `scope:target` is the new best friend. Vanilla sends a toast, removes a potential friend relation with the target and removes a dead best friend modifier from the target. With Ritualised Friendship, it gives both characters a strong hook on each other, if they do not have one yet. The input cuts the script off.

label: Blood brother relation set
summary: Runs when two characters become blood brothers.
details: The root is the character and `scope:target` the new blood brother. Vanilla sends a toast, gives both a memory, creates an alliance between them and gives each a blood brother hook on the other. In a hidden effect it also marks the root's family (children and primary spouse) for the blood brother close family opinion. The input cuts the script off.

label: Crush relation set
summary: Runs when a character develops a crush on another character.
details: The root has the crush and `scope:target` is the object of it. The vanilla comment says crushes are one-sided, and only the root gets a memory of it.

label: Disciple relation set
summary: Runs when a character gets a disciple.
details: Vanilla checks if the root now has enough disciples for the family accomplishment about disciples. If so, it marks that accomplishment for the head of the root's house, through their domicile.

label: Elder relation set
summary: Runs when a character gets an elder.
details: The root is the disciple and `scope:target` the new elder. Vanilla makes the root a fellow disciple of the elder's other disciples. It also marks the family accomplishment about disciples for the head of the elder's house, if the elder has enough disciples.

label: Friend relation set
summary: Runs when two characters become friends.
details: The root is the character and `scope:target` the new friend. Vanilla sends a toast, removes a potential friend relation, runs the friendly counsel skill gain and confidants update for both, applies decentralized rule friend modifiers to the root and gives both a memory. In struggle phases with the matching parameter, befriending someone of another faith or culture gives both prestige scaled by the target's title tier. The input cuts the script off.

label: Grudge relation set
summary: Runs when a character starts holding a grudge against another character.
details: The root holds the grudge and `scope:target` is who it is held against. Vanilla sends a toast and gives the root a memory of it.

label: Guardian relation set
summary: Runs when a ward gets a guardian.
details: The root is the ward and `scope:target` is the guardian. If the ward has a liege and both are in a struggle phase that applies a truce when sending wards, a 10 year truce is set between the playable guardian and the ward's liege, and a struggle catalyst may fire. The comment in the vanilla file says it is fired when the ward removes the relation, which does not match the script or the name.

label: Lover relation set
summary: Runs when two characters become lovers.
details: The root is the character and `scope:target` the new lover. Vanilla sends a toast, runs effects that may give incest and homosexual secrets, removes a potential lover relation and fires struggle catalysts. If either lover is a child, an event fires after one day. Both get a memory of becoming lovers.

label: Nemesis relation set
summary: Runs when a character gets a nemesis.
details: The root is the character and `scope:target` the new nemesis. Vanilla fires struggle catalysts, sends a toast, removes a potential rival relation, gives both a memory, applies harrying logic and clears grudges between the two. Clans lose unity through a medium unity loss. It also has house relation logic that the input does not show in full.

label: Rival relation set
summary: Runs when a character gets a rival.
details: The root is the character and `scope:target` the new rival. Vanilla fires struggle catalysts, sends a toast, removes a potential rival relation, gives both a memory, applies harrying logic and clears grudges between the two. Clans lose unity through a medium unity loss. It also has a hostage story cycle part that the input does not show in full.

label: Soulmate relation set
summary: Runs when two characters become soulmates.
details: The root is the character and `scope:target` the new soulmate. Vanilla sends a toast, removes a potential lover relation, fires struggle catalysts and gives both a memory. If one of them has a promoted legend, that character gets a legend spread event, with the other saved as `scope:soulmate`. The rest of the script is not shown in the input.

label: Siege completed
summary: Runs when a siege completes and a barony is occupied.
details: The root is the occupant. Scopes: `scope:barony`, `scope:county`, `scope:previous_controller` and `scope:war`, plus a list `occupied_baronies`. It does not fire when the province owner retakes it, because `on_liberation_siege_completion` covers that. Vanilla fires events about notifying holders, capturing prisoners, stealing artifacts and reinforcing rebels, and rites can give piety and reduce county development. The input cuts the script off.

label: Siege loots a holding
summary: Runs when a siege loots a holding.
details: The root is the sieging character. Scopes: `scope:barony`, `scope:county` and `scope:previous_controller`. Vanilla replenishes the troops of landless adventurer armies in the province, gives provisions with the Strict Organization perk, and marks the province as recently looted for 5 years. It also gives extra gold if the character has a master of spoils camp officer. The input cuts the script off.

label: Specific birthday
summary: Picks the first valid one of the 3rd, 6th, 10th, 15th and 16th birthday on_actions.
details: The root is the character. Vanilla defines it with a list of those five on_actions in that order and runs only the first one that is valid. The game does not fire it from code, so script is expected to fire it; the input does not show where.

label: Stress level 1 reached
summary: Runs when a character reaches stress level 1.
details: The root is the character. It only runs if the character has not recently hit a stress threshold, which stops several mental breaks on one day. Vanilla fires the stress management event, then after 3 days a mental break event (or a prison one). It also sets an achievement flag, plays stress music and gives a 15% chance to flip a sinful trait with a certain personal tenet.

label: Stress level 2 reached
summary: Runs when a character reaches stress level 2.
details: The root is the character. Like level 1 it is blocked when the character recently hit a stress threshold, and fires the stress management event and, after 3 days, a mental break event (or a prison one). It sets an achievement flag but plays no music, and gives a 25% chance to flip a sinful trait with a certain personal tenet.

label: Stress level 3 reached
summary: Runs when a character reaches stress level 3.
details: The root is the character. Like level 2 it is blocked when the character recently hit a stress threshold, and fires the stress management event and, after 3 days, a mental break event (or a prison one). It sets an achievement flag and gives a 50% chance to flip a sinful trait with a certain personal tenet.

label: Stress level 4 reached
summary: Runs when a character reaches stress level 4.
details: The root is the character. It is blocked when the character recently hit a stress threshold. Vanilla fires the event that resets stress at 400, which triggers its own mental breaks, sets an achievement flag and always flips a sinful trait with a certain personal tenet.

label: Stress level reduced
summary: Runs when a character's stress level goes down.
details: The root is the character. Vanilla shows a toast that a stress level was lost. With a certain personal tenet, and at most once per year, it also gives piety and spiritual fulfillment.

label: Title destroyed
summary: Runs when a title is destroyed.
details: The root is the holder before the destruction and `scope:landed_title` the title destroyed. It does not give `scope:transfer_type`. Vanilla first removes a special administrative title the destroyed title points to. Then it applies the first case that fits: changing the government of an independent administrative ruler left without a kingdom or higher title, removing a destroyed duchy from the duchy tally list, removing a holder who lost their last empire from the empire holder list, a message for the fall of the Latin Empire, or a collapse counter for Byzantium. The input cuts the script off, so more cases may follow.

label: Title gained
summary: Runs when a title is transferred to a new holder.
details: The root is the new holder. `scope:title` is the title that changes hands and `scope:previous_holder` the former holder, who might be dead. The script also reads `scope:transfer_type`, for example for conquest by holy war or inheritance. Vanilla refreshes the state rite after a holy war conquest, handles cardinal titles and the Christian church situation, and sets ecclesiastical government for some adventurers and titles. It also seeds monk courtiers in some cases. The input cuts the script off, so more may follow.
